files.header:
=============================================================================
 Retail Application Scorecard  (RCS-APP-02)
 Owner      : Retail Credit Risk Modelling
 Purpose    : Probability of default (12m) for unsecured personal loan applications
 Developed  : 2019   Last validated: 2021-03-15
 Data       : data/processed/german_credit_{train,test}.csv  (public UCI German Credit,
              used here as a stand-in for the bank's application data)
 =============================================================================
 Method: weight-of-evidence (WoE) binning + logistic regression, scaled to points.
   1. Numeric variables with more than 10 distinct values are cut into 5 quantile bins
      (quantile type 7, breaks from the training data, outer breaks set to -Inf/Inf).
      All other variables are treated as categorical, one bin per level.
   2. WoE per bin = ln( ((n_good + 0.5) / total_good) / ((n_bad + 0.5) / total_bad) ).
      Information value IV = sum((dist_good - dist_bad) * WoE) with the same smoothing.
   3. Variables with IV >= 0.02 are kept. Protected attributes are never candidates.
   4. Logistic regression of bad (1 = default) on the WoE-transformed variables.
   5. Score = offset + factor * ln(odds_good), PDO 20, 600 points at good:bad odds 50:1.
 Usage: Rscript models/credit_scorecard/scorecard.R [data_dir] [out_dir]
 =============================================================================

purpose_and_use.text: Estimates the 12-month probability of default (PD) for unsecured personal loan applications (application scorecard RCS-APP-02, owned by Retail Credit Risk Modelling, risk tier high per inventory). The code outputs a PD and a points score per application. IMPORTANT: the code header states the public UCI German Credit dataset is used 'as a stand-in for the bank's application data', so the artefacts reviewed are not built on bank production data. How scores are used downstream (cut-offs, decisioning, pricing) is not stated in the material.

evidence.quote: Purpose    : Probability of default (12m) for unsecured personal loan applications
used here as a stand-in for the bank's application data

data.text: Inputs are data/processed/german_credit_train.csv and german_credit_test.csv (public UCI German Credit, processed). Target is 'bad' (1 = default, 0 = good). Reference metrics show a fixed split of 700 training and 300 test records, each with a 30% bad rate (so the split appears stratified, though the splitting code is not in the material; no validation or out-of-time sample). Excluded from candidates: id, the target, and protected/sensitive attributes personal_status_sex, sex, age_group, foreign_worker. All remaining columns are candidate variables. Note that 'age' is NOT excluded and ends up as a selected model variable. Data provenance, split method and the observation/performance window are not documented.

methodology.text: Weight-of-evidence (WoE) binning followed by logistic regression, scaled to points. (1) Numeric variables with more than 10 distinct values are cut into 5 quantile bins (type 7, breaks from training data, outer breaks -Inf/Inf); other variables are categorical with one bin per level. (2) WoE per bin = ln(((n_good+0.5)/total_good)/((n_bad+0.5)/total_bad)); IV computed with the same smoothing. (3) Variables with IV >= 0.02 are retained (14 selected; all non-excluded candidates appear to pass or the selected list is as shown in metrics.json). (4) Logistic regression (glm, binomial) of bad on the WoE-transformed variables, no regularisation or stepwise selection. (5) Scaling: factor = PDO/ln(2), offset = 600 - factor*ln(50), score = offset + factor*ln((1-PD)/PD), i.e. 600 points at good:bad odds 50:1 with PDO 20. All fitted WoE coefficients are negative except woe_job (+0.657, std error 0.670, not significant), which has a counter-intuitive sign for a WoE-transformed variable and indicates multicollinearity or instability. Several coefficients (credit_amount, other_debtors, property, age, housing, job) have standard errors comparable to or larger than the estimate. DOCUMENTATION CONFLICT: the 2019 methodology note describes four coarse-classed characteristics with 4 bins each, dummy-coded logistic regression, and scaling to 500 points at odds 20:1 with 25 PDO. The code (which prevails) uses all candidate variables with 5 quantile bins, WoE transformation, IV selection, and 600/50:1/PDO 20.

evidence.quote: 4. Logistic regression of bad (1 = default) on the WoE-transformed variables.
5. Score = offset + factor * ln(odds_good), PDO 20, 600 points at good:bad odds 50:1.
The scorecard uses four coarse-classed characteristics: checking account status, loan
at odds 20:1 with 25 points to double the odds.

implementation.text: R (version 4.1.2 recorded in metrics.json); jsonlite is the only library loaded, with base R glm for estimation and hand-written AUC, KS and WoE functions. set.seed(42) is set (the code itself contains no random operations: quantile binning and glm are deterministic). Run with: Rscript models/credit_scorecard/scorecard.R [data_dir] [out_dir]; defaults are data/processed and artifacts/reference/credit_scorecard. Outputs: bins.csv (per-variable bin WoE/IV/selection), coefficients.csv (estimates and standard errors only), predictions_test.csv (id, bad, pd, score for the test set) and metrics.json (settings, selected variables, breaks, metrics). Treatment of unseen categorical levels at scoring: assigned WoE 0 (neutral). Missing values in input are not explicitly handled; a missing numeric value would produce NA bin and then WoE 0, but this is not tested or documented. Predictions on the training set are computed but not saved.

evidence.quote: w[is.na(w)] <- 0  # level not seen in training: neutral WoE

performance.text: Reference outputs (metrics.json) report: Train (n=700, bad rate 30%): AUC 0.8171, Gini 0.6341, KS 0.4952. Test (n=300, bad rate 30%): AUC 0.8010, Gini 0.6019, KS 0.5063. The small train-to-test AUC drop (~0.016) suggests limited overfitting on this sample. No calibration results, PD accuracy tests (e.g. Hosmer-Lemeshow, binomial), stability (PSI), score-band analysis, challenger comparison, or bias/fairness testing exist in the material. With only 300 test records (about 90 bads) the test metrics carry wide sampling uncertainty. Metrics are on the stand-in public dataset and cannot be read as bank portfolio performance.

monitoring_and_governance.text: Owner: Retail Credit Risk Modelling. Developed 2019; last validated 2021-03-15 (internal model validation team per the methodology note). Inventory classifies the model as high risk tier, for which validation is required every 12 months, so validation is roughly 68 months overdue; the methodology note (June 2019) is about 89 months old against a 24-month limit and describes a materially different model from the code, so the validated model may not be the current code, or the documentation was never updated. No monitoring (PSI, performance tracking, recalibration triggers), no change log, no approval/sign-off record, and no validation report are in the material. Under PRA SS1/23 this record should be treated as non-compliant until revalidation and documentation update are completed.

transformations.description: Read train/test CSVs; candidates are all columns except id, bad, personal_status_sex, sex, age_group, foreign_worker.

Numeric variables with more than 10 distinct values get 5 bins from training quantiles (type 7), duplicates removed, outer breaks set to -Inf/Inf; cut with right=TRUE, include.lowest=TRUE. Other variables use one bin per level.
transformations.evidence: br <- unique(quantile(x, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = N_BINS + 1), type = 7, names = FALSE))

transformations.description: WoE = ln(((n_good+0.5)/total_good)/((n_bad+0.5)/total_bad)) per bin; IV = sum((dist_good - dist_bad)*WoE).
Replace each selected variable by its bin WoE (woe_<var>); levels unseen in training get WoE 0.
transformations.evidence: w[is.na(w)] <- 0  # level not seen in training: neutral WoE

transformations.description: glm binomial of bad on all WoE columns; PD = predicted probability of default.
transformations.evidence: fit <- glm(train[[TARGET]] ~ ., data = X_train, family = binomial())

transformations.description: factor = 20/ln(2); offset = 600 - factor*ln(50); score = offset + factor*ln((1-PD)/PD).
transformations.evidence: to_score   <- function(pd) offset_pts + factor_pts * log((1 - pd) / pd)

transformations.description: AUC (rank-based), Gini = 2*AUC-1 and KS computed on train and test; writes bins.csv, coefficients.csv, predictions_test.csv, metrics.json.
transformations.evidence: metrics[[s]] <- list(n = length(y), bad_rate = mean(y), auc = a, gini = 2 * a - 1, ks = ks(y, p))

limitations.text: Documentation is materially inconsistent with code (variable set, bins, estimation form, scaling constants); the 2019 note cannot be relied on and the validated model may differ from the current code.
limitations.evidence: The scorecard uses four coarse-classed characteristics: checking account status, loan

limitations.text: Validation is overdue (last 2021-03-15 against a 12-month cycle for high tier) and documentation is stale (June 2019).
Model is demonstrated on a 1,000-record public dataset (300 test records), so metrics have wide uncertainty and are not evidence of performance on the bank's portfolio.
No calibration assessment: the scaling uses logistic PD directly with no check that PDs match observed default rates; no through-the-cycle or downturn adjustment is described.

Counter-intuitive positive sign on woe_job and large standard errors on several coefficients (credit_amount, other_debtors, property, age, housing, job) indicate possible multicollinearity or weak contribution; no sign-constraint or collinearity checks in code.
Continuous 'age' is used as a model input while age_group is treated as protected; potential age-related fairness/conduct concern with no fairness testing documented.
No explicit handling or testing of missing values, outliers, or reject inference (only accepted-loan outcomes are implied).

unknowns: Origin of the bank's actual development data, sample window, performance/default definition and observation period for the 12-month PD.
How the train/test split was produced (stratification, seed, time basis); the splitting code is not provided.
Which variables were evaluated but dropped by the IV >= 0.02 rule (the selected list is known; bins.csv content was not provided in the material).
How scores and PDs are used in decisioning (cut-offs, pricing, overrides, policy rules) and whether the model is in production.
Whether the 2021 validation covered the current code or the 2019 coarse-class model, and the outcome/findings of that validation.
Ongoing monitoring arrangements (PSI, back-testing, recalibration thresholds) and the current approval status.
Calibration of PD to the bank's long-run default rate and any margin of conservatism or regulatory adjustments.
Fairness/conduct risk assessment and justification for use of age as an input.
Version control, change history, and the reason documentation diverged from code.
Treatment of missing data and reject inference in production.
